## How the plans are kept

The plans are generated, not edited: `dart run tool/testplan_report.dart`
writes, from the bridges and the corpus,

- `testplan_<library>.md` — every name the bridges register for a library,
  with its tier, its status and the scripts that use it;
- `testplan_essential.md`, `testplan_important.md`, `testplan_secondary.md`,
  `testplan_hardly_relevant.md` — the same rows by tier;
- the Coverage block above.

The one hand-maintained input is the tiering: the tables of
`testpriority_<library>.md` (class and description under an `## Essential`,
`## Important`, `## Secondary` or `## Hardly Relevant` heading). A bridged
class no priority file names is Hardly Relevant. Re-run the tool after adding
or changing a corpus script, a driver or a priority row, or after regenerating
the bridges; `test/testplan_fresh_test.dart` (in `run_guard_tests.sh`) fails
while a committed plan differs from what the tool writes, or while a priority
row names a class the bridges do not register.

## Flutter 3.47 inventory

The corpus scripts and the per-library testplans were written against Flutter
3.41.3. The bridges are generated on Flutter 3.47.9. Measured 2026-11-10:

- **18 bridged names are new in Flutter 3.47** (not declared in Flutter
  3.41.3) and each has a script, run by `flutter_extended_25_test.dart` in
  both twins: cupertino CupertinoMenuAnchor, CupertinoMenuDivider,
  CupertinoMenuEntry, CupertinoMenuItem; dart:ui DisplayCornerRadii,
  HitTestRequest, HitTestResponse, UniformArray, UniformMat2Slot,
  UniformMat3Slot, UniformType; gestures NativeHitTestTarget; material
  ShapedInputBorder, TabBarScrollController; rendering ScrollCacheExtent;
  services TextInputStyle, UiKitViewGestureBlockingPolicy; widgets
  ContextMenuButtonKind. All 18 are exercised (✅ in their library's
  testplan). UniformMat4Slot, also new, is named only in a string of a
  script, so it is not exercised (⬜ in `testplan_dart_ui.md`).
- **RefreshIndicatorStatus** (material), which existed in 3.41.3, has no
  script (⬜ in `testplan_material.md`).
- **27 names Flutter 3.47 declares are not bridged**, because no library the
  bridges are generated from exports them: the windowing classes
  (`src/widgets/_window*.dart`), the accessibility evaluations
  (`src/widgets/_accessibility_evaluations.dart`), ErrorToConsoleDumper
  (`src/foundation/_error_dumper_*.dart`), the `Console` extension type of
  `src/web.dart`, and MultiPreviewThemeData (`widget_previews.dart`, not among
  the generated barrels).

Method: the names come from the bridge files' `classSourceUris()` /
`enumSourceUris()` maps; "declared in a release" is a `class`, `enum`,
`mixin` or `extension type` declaration under `packages/flutter/lib` or
`engine/src/flutter/lib/ui` at that release's tag. Whether a class is
exercised follows the generated plans' rule (named in a running script's
code), stricter than the name merely appearing in a script file.

## Test Script Template

```dart
// D4rt test script: Tests <ClassName> from <module>
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

dynamic build(BuildContext context) {
  // Test marker for validation
  print('<ClassName> test executing');
  
  // Create and configure the widget/object
  final widget = <ConstructorCall>();
  
  // Print validation markers
  print('<ClassName> created successfully');
  
  return widget;
}
```

## Validation Criteria

Each test should verify:
1. ✅ Class is accessible (can be referenced)
2. ✅ Constructor(s) work without errors
3. ✅ Basic properties can be set
4. ✅ Widget renders (for widget classes)
5. ✅ Print output is captured correctly
